title: Ice Protection — Wing Anti-Ice Valve — Reprofiled Butterfly and Non-Contact Feedback

issue.reason: Issue C. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Line-station replaceable rework of the wing anti-ice valve, giving the butterfly a relieved trailing edge and a cold clearance and replacing the wiper track feedback by a magnetic sensor outside the hot gas path.

sections.planning_reason: Intermittent wing anti-ice fault messages accumulated at 1.4 per 1 000 flight hours, almost all in the climb between flight level 180 and flight level 280, and nearly two thirds of removed valves passed shop acceptance test. Instrumented flight showed the butterfly binding against the housing as the duct heats unevenly, and the potentiometric feedback track wearing at the two commanded positions the valve actually uses. Operators were carrying an average of 2.3 spare valves per line station for a fault that in most cases did not exist.
sections.description: The butterfly is reprofiled with a relieved trailing edge and the housing bore is opened to a 0.08 mm cold clearance. The redundant heat exchanger is deleted from the valve assembly and the bleed take-off is blanked. Position feedback moves from a wiper track to a non-contact magnetic sensor mounted outside the hot gas path, on a bracket retained by the new screw and washer set.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Extend the slats and install the slat locks. WARNING: DO NOT WORK IN THE SLAT AREA WITHOUT THE SLAT LOCKS INSTALLED. Get access at the wing leading edge in zones 512 and 611 and in the slat area in zone 551. Remove the wing anti-ice valve from the duct. Remove the outboard heat exchanger kit D3010115902013 from the valve assembly and blank the take-off port. Install the reprofiled butterfly from the kit and check the cold clearance with feeler gauges at four positions. Remove the wiper track feedback and install the magnetic sensor bracket with countersunk screws EN229422-9A and washers EN906402-5B, discarding the previous screw set AGS997812-2C. Install the valve on the duct. Re-wire the left-hand switch position 6HA to the three-wire feedback interface using the harness adapter supplied in the kit. Do AMM-S-30-10-11-700-015-A as the wing anti-ice operational test, including a full travel sweep with the feedback recorded. Remove the slat locks and retract the slats. Record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to all twin-engine aircraft including the Evo variants delivered before the production cut-in at MSN S01798. The valve can be modified on wing; the aircraft does not need to be in a hangar and no de-fuelling is required.
sections.material_note: Kit K3010-1011-01 covers one valve and contains the butterfly, the magnetic sensor, the bracket, the harness adapter and the fastener set. Two kits are needed per aircraft. Lead time is twelve weeks. The removed heat exchangers are scrapped locally.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next removal of the wing anti-ice valve for any reason, or within 36 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.

revision_history.reason: Effectivity extended to the Evo variants; harness adapter added to the kit
Cold clearance check made a four-position measurement after two operators reported a single-point check passing on an out-of-round housing
